Cause: Person attached to the open breadboard or AD8232 lead cable
Control: Human attachment is prohibited; use an ECG simulator for waveform-acquisition exercises

Cause: USB, charger, mains-powered computer, oscilloscope, or other externally powered equipment connected while the AD8232 simulator lead interface is attached
Control: Disconnect the AD8232 lead cable before USB programming, charging, serial debugging, or connection to externally powered test equipment

Cause: Open breadboard and loose jumper wiring
Control: Supervised bench work only; inspect exposed conductors, jumper security, cable condition, and ground continuity before operation

Cause: Wrong polarity, unstable regulator output, incompatible charger, or unprotected cell
Control: Use a protected 1S battery-derived source; set and verify the regulator output at 3.3 V before connecting modules

Cause: No documented certified patient-isolation barrier or leakage-current validation
Control: No human attachment; no medical-device or electrical-safety compliance claim

Cause: Qualitative waveform or raw ADC counts treated as calibrated or diagnostic measurements
Control: No clinical interpretation; retain raw ADC counts unless an independent calibration experiment has been performed; use simulator-based exercises

Cause: SD write interruption or unexpected power loss
Control: Use storage-status reporting, periodic file flush, file inspection, and preservation of raw files after each run

Cause: Loose or open simulator lead, poor ground, or unstable breadboard connection
Control: Use LO+/LO- status logging, staged troubleshooting, and simulator/open-lead testing
